<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{rn}
  Let $M,N\subset\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ be compact convex sets such that
  $\mu\perp\nu$ whenever $\mu\in M$ and $\nu\in N$.
  Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $g\in \mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])$ such that
  $|\mu(1-g)|<\varepsilon$ for every $\mu\in M$ and $|\nu(g)|<\varepsilon$ for every $\nu\in N$.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Replacing $M$ by $\{\mu_1-\mu_2: \mu_1,\mu_2\in M\}$ if necessary, we may assume that
  $-\mu\in M$ whenever $\mu\in M$. Similarly, we may assume that $-\nu\in N$ whenever $\nu\in N$.
  
  
  Define $f\colon (M\times N)\times \mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])\to\mathbb{R}$ by
  $f((\mu,\nu),g):=\mu(1-g)+\nu(g)$.
  Then $M\times N$ is a compact convex subset of $\mathcal{M}_s(X)\times\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$
  and $f$ satisfies the assumptions of various extensions of the
  von Neumann minimax theorem (see, for example \cite[page 116]{G}, \cite[Theorem 2]{KF} or \cite[Corollary 3.3]{S}).
  Hence
  \begin{equation}\label{rn.E1}
    \adjustlimits\sup_{\mu,\nu}\inf_{g} \mu(1-g)+\nu(g) = \adjustlimits\inf_g\sup_{\mu,\nu} \mu(1-g)+\nu(g).
  \end{equation}
  Since the left side of \eqref{rn.E1} is less or equal to zero, so is its right side.
  Thus, given $\varepsilon>0$ there is $g\in\mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])$ such that
  $\mu(1-g)+\nu(g)<\varepsilon$ for every $\mu\in M$ and $\nu\in N$. Choosing $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}$
  such that $\sigma\mu(1-g) = |\mu(1-g)|$ and $\tau\nu(g)=|\nu(g)|$ and recalling that
  $\sigma\mu\in M$ and $\tau\nu\in N$, we get  $|\mu(1-g)|+|\nu(g)|<\varepsilon$, implying the statement.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{r1}
  Let $M,N \subset\mathcal{M}(X)$ be compact convex sets such that $\mu\perp\nu$ whenever $\mu\in M$ and $\nu\in N$.
  Then there are disjoint $Z_\sigma$ sets $B_M,B_N$ such that every $\mu\in M$ sits on $B_M$
  and every $\nu\in N$ sits on $B_N$.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $g_n\in \mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])$ come from \Cref{rn} with $\varepsilon_n:=4^{-n}$ and put $E_n:=\{x: g_n(x)\ge 1- 2^{-n}\}$
  and $F_n:=\{x: g_n(x)\le 2^{-n}\}$. Then $E_n$ and $F_n$ are zero-sets
  such that $\mu(X\setminus E_n)\le 2^n\mu(1-g_n)\le 2^{-n}$ for $\mu\in M$, and 
  $\nu(X\setminus F_n)\le 2^n\nu(g_n)\le 2^{-n}$ for $\nu\in N$.
  Hence it suffices to let
  \[B_M:=\bigcup_{k=1}^\infty \bigcap_{n=k}^\infty E_n\text{ and }
    B_N:=\bigcup_{k=1}^\infty \bigcap_{n=k}^\infty F_n.\qedhere\]
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{rl0}
  Let $M\subset\mathcal{M}_s(X)$ satisfying \ref{sm} and $N \subset\mathcal{M}(X)$ be compact convex sets
  such that $\mu\perp\nu$ whenever $\mu\in M$ and $\nu\in N$.
  Then there is a $Z_\sigma$ set $B$ such that every $\mu\in M$ sits on $X\setminus B$
  and every $\nu\in N$ sits on $B$.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Choose $h_1,h_2,\ldots\in \mathcal{C}(X,[-1,1])$ with
  $\|\mu\| =\sup \{\mu(h_i): i\in\mathbb{N}\}$ for every $\mu\in M$,  such that in the
  sequence $h_i$, $i=1,2,\dots$ each element appears infinitely often.

  For each $i$ use \Cref{rn}
  with the sets $M_i:=\{h_i\mu: \nu\in N\}$ and $N$, and with $\varepsilon=4^{-i}$,
  to find $g_{i}\in \mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])$ such that
  $\mu(h_i(1-g_i))< 4^{-i}$ for every $\mu\in M$ and
  $\nu(g_i)<4^{-i}$ for every $\nu\in N$.
  Put
  \[D_i:=\{x\in X: g_{i}(x) \le 2^{-i}\},\
    B_j:=\bigcap_{i=j}^\infty D_{i}\text{ and } B:=\bigcup_{j=1}^\infty B_j.\]

  For any $\nu\in N$ we get
  $\nu(X\setminus D_i)\le 2^{i}\nu(g_i) \le 2^{-i}$, hence $\nu(X\setminus B_j)\le 2^{-j+1}$,
  and $\nu(X\setminus B)=0$. Hence $\nu$ sits on $B$.

  It remains to show that every $\mu\in M$ sits on $X\setminus B$, i.e, that $|\mu|(B)=0$.
  For this, given $j\in \mathbb{N}$, find $i>j$ such that $\|\mu\|-\mu(h_i)< 4^{-j-1}$. Since
  $|h_ig_i|\le g_i$, $\mu(h_ig_i)\le |\mu|(g)$, and hence
  \[|\mu|(1-g_i)=\|\mu\|-|\mu|(g_i)\le 4^{-i}+\mu(h_i)-\mu(h_ig_i)\le 2\star4^{-j-1}.\]
  Since $1-g_i\ge 1/2$ on $D_i$, we see that $|\mu|(B_j)\le |\mu|(D_i)\le 4^{-j}$
  for every~$j$. Since $B_j\subset B_{j+1}$, this shows
   $|\mu|(B_j)=0$ for every~$j$ and so $|\mu|(B)=0$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- dfn-1: body_md -->
\label{ca0}
  A subset $U$ of a locally convex space $T$ is said to be convexly analytic if
  there is an usco mapping 
  $\phi:\mathcal{N}\to T$
  such that $U=\phi(\mathcal{N})$ and the closed convex hull of $\phi(K)$ is contained in $U$ for every compact $K\subset\mathcal{N}$.
<!-- end dfn-1 -->
<!-- obs-1: body_md -->
\label{a1}
   Suppose $\phi$ is an usco map of $\mathcal{N}$ to $\mathcal{M}_s(X)$.
   Then the map $\psi$ assigning to $\sigma\in\mathcal{N}$ the closed convex hull of $\phi(\mathcal{N}_\sigma)$ is usco.
<!-- end obs-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
From the above discussion we see that $\psi$ is compact valued. Hence we just need to show that it is upper semicontinuous.
  For that, assume $\sigma\in\mathcal{N}$ and $G\supset \psi(\sigma)$ is open. Since $\psi(\sigma)$ is compact,
  there is an open convex set $V\ni 0$ such that $\overline{V+\psi(\sigma)}\subset G$. Then $V+\psi(\sigma)$ is an open set
  containing the compact set $\phi(\mathcal{N}_\sigma)$, hence there is $k$ such that
  $\phi(\mathcal{N}_{\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k})\subset V+\psi(\sigma)$.
  Since $\overline{V+\psi(\sigma)}$ is closed and convex,
  we get $\psi(\tau)\subset \overline{V+\psi(\sigma)}\subset G$ for every $\tau\in\mathcal{N}_{\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k}$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- dfn-2: body_md -->
\label{defsep}
  A measure $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is said to be $\varepsilon$-separated from a set $N\subset\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$, where $\varepsilon\ge 0$, if there is
  a Baire measurable function $f\colon X\to[0,1]$ such that
  $|\mu|(1-f)\le\varepsilon$ and $|\nu|(f)\le\varepsilon+2\|\nu^-\|$ for every $\nu\in N$.
<!-- end dfn-2 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{s1}
  Let $N_1\subset N_2\subset\dots\subset\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$,
  $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\ldots\ge 0$, $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_s(X)$ be $\varepsilon_i$\nobreakdash-separated from $N_i$ for each $i$,
  and $\varepsilon:=\limsup_{i\to\infty} \varepsilon_i$. Then
  $\mu$ is $\varepsilon$\nobreakdash-separated from 
  $\bigcup_{i=1}^\infty N_i$.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $\mu$ be $\varepsilon_i$-separated from $N_i$ by a function $f_i$. Considered in $L_2(|\mu|)$,
  the sequence $f_i$ contains a weakly convergent subsequence and so by
  Mazur's Lemma there are norm convergent convex combinations
  $g_j:=\sum_{i=j}^\infty c_{i,j} f_i$. Hence there is a
  subsequence $g_{j_k}$ of $g_j$ which converges $\mu$ almost everywhere.
  Let $E$ be the (necessarily Baire) set of $x$ for which $g_{j_k}(x)$ converges. Define
  $h_k(x)=g_{j_k}(x)$ for $x\in E$ and 
  $h_k(x)=0$ otherwise, and put $f(x):=\lim_{k\to\infty} h_k(x)$.
  Then $f$ is a well defined Baire measurable map of $X$ to $[0,1]$,
  \begin{align*}
    |\mu|(1-f)&=
              \lim_{k\to\infty} |\mu|(1-g_{j_k})
              \le \limsup_{i\to\infty} |\mu|(1-f_i) \le 
              \limsup_{i\to\infty}\varepsilon_i=\varepsilon\\
    \intertext{and for every $\nu\in M$,}
    |\nu|(f)&=\lim_{k\to\infty} |\nu|(h_k)\le \limsup_{j\to\infty}|\nu|(g_j)\le
      \limsup_{i\to\infty} |\nu|(f_i)\\
           &\le \limsup_{i\to\infty}\varepsilon_i +2\|\nu^-\| =\varepsilon+2\|\nu^-\|.\qedhere
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{T-0}
  Suppose $N\subset\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is convexly analytic and $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is such that
  $\mu\perp\nu$ for every $\nu\in N$.
  Then $\mu$ sits on a Baire set $B\subset X$ such that
  $|\nu|(B)\le 2\|\nu^-\|$
  for every $\nu\in N$.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Our goal is to show that for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\mu$ is $\varepsilon$-separated from $N$. 
  Then \Cref{s1} with $N_i:=N$ and $\varepsilon_i:=1/i$ implies that
  $\mu$ is $0$-separated from~$N$. Hence there is a Baire measurable function $f\in\mathcal{C}(X,[0,1])$
  such that $|\mu|(1-f)=0$ and $|\nu|(f)\le 2\nu^-(f)$, and we see that
  the statement holds with $B:=\{x:f(x)= 1\}$.

  Suppose, for a contradiction, that for some $\varepsilon>0$, $\mu$ is not $\varepsilon$-separated from~$N$. By \Cref{ca0}, $N=\phi(\mathcal{N})$,
  where $\phi:\mathcal{N}\to\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is usco and such that for every $\sigma\in\mathcal{N}$ the set $C_\sigma:=\overline{\mathrm{conv}}\,\phi(\mathcal{N}_\sigma)$ is
  a convex subset of~$N$.
  Since $\phi(\mathcal{N}_1)\subset\phi(\mathcal{N}_2)\subset\dots$ and
  $N=\bigcup_{\sigma_1=1}^\infty \phi(\mathcal{N}_{\sigma_1})$, by \Cref{s1} there is $\sigma_1\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $\mu$ is not $\varepsilon$-separated from
  $\phi(\mathcal{N}_{\sigma_1})$. Continuing recursively, we find $\sigma_k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $\mu$ is not $\varepsilon$-separated
  from $\phi(\mathcal{N}_{\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k})$ for each $k=1,2,\dots$.
  Letting $\sigma:=(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\dots)$ and recalling that $C_\sigma:=\overline{\mathrm{conv}}\,\phi(\mathcal{N}_\sigma)$ is
  a compact and convex subset of $N$,
  we use \Cref{rn} with $M:=\{|\mu|\}$ to find $f\in C(X,[0,1])$
  such that $|\mu|(1-f)<\varepsilon$ and $\nu(f)<\varepsilon$ for every $\nu\in C_\sigma$.
  Since the map $\nu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)\to\nu(f)$ is continuous,
  $G:=\{\nu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}: \nu(f)<\varepsilon\}$ is an open set containing $\phi(\mathcal{N}_\sigma)$.
  Hence the upper semicontinuity of $\phi$ implies 
  that there is $k$ such that $\nu \in G$ for every $\nu\in \phi(\mathcal{N}_{\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k})$. 
  It follows that $|\nu|(f)=\nu(f)+2\nu^-(f)\le\varepsilon+2\|\nu^-\|$ for every such $\nu$, 
  and we conclude that $\mu$
  is $\varepsilon$-separated from $\phi(\mathcal{N}_{\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k})$, which is the desired contradiction.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{T-1}
  Suppose $N\subset\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is convexly analytic, $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is such that
  $\mu\perp\nu$ for every $\nu\in N$ and $h\in\mathcal{C}(X,[-1,1])$.
  Then $\mu$ sits on a Baire set $B\subset X$ such that
  $|\nu|(B)\le 2(\|\nu\|-\nu(h))$
  for every $\nu\in N$.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
By \Cref{T-0}, since $\{h\nu: \nu\in N\}$ is convexly analytic, $\mu$ sits on a Baire set $B$
  such that $|h\nu|(B)\le 2\|(h\nu)^-\|=\|h\nu\|-\nu(h)\le \|\nu\|-\nu(h)$.
  Hence
  \begin{align*}
    |\nu|(B)&= |\nu|(X)-|\nu|(X\setminus B)\le |\nu|(X)-(h\nu)(X\setminus B)\\
            & \le \|\nu\|-\nu(h)+|h\nu|(B)\le 2(\|\nu\|-\nu(h)).\qedhere
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{T-2}
  Suppose $N\subset\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is convexly analytic, $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is such that
  $\mu\perp\nu$ for every $\nu\in N$ and $H\subset\mathcal{C}(X,[-1,1])$ is countable.
  Then $\mu$ sits on a Baire set $B\subset X$ such that
  $|\nu|(B)\le 2\inf \{\|\nu\|-\nu(h): h\in H\}$
  for every $\nu\in N$.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By \Cref{T-1}, for every $h\in H$ there is a a Baire set $B_h\subset X$ such that
  $\mu$ sits on $B_h$ and
  $|\nu|(B_h)\le \|\nu\|-\nu(h)$
  for every $\nu\in N$. Since $H$ is countable, the set $B:=\bigcap_{h\in H} B_h$ has
  the stated properties.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{T1}
  Suppose a convexly analytic set $N\subset\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ satisfies \ref{sm} and $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ is such that
  $\mu\perp\nu$ for every $\nu\in N$.
  Then $\mu$ sits on a Baire set $B\subset X$ such that every $\nu\in N$ sits on $X\setminus B$.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{T-4}
  Let $N\subset\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ be an analytic set satisfying \ref{sm}. Then for every $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_s(X)$
  there are 
  a Baire function $g:X\to\mathbb{R}$, a Baire set $B\subset X$ and $\lambda\in\mathcal{P}(N)$ such that $\int\|\nu\|\,d\lambda(\nu)<\infty$,
  $g(x)=0$ for $x\in B$, $\int|g(x)|\,d|\hat\lambda|(x)<\infty$,
  $|\nu|(B)=0$ for every $\nu\in N$, and for every Baire set $E\subset X$, 
  \begin{equation}
    \label{E}\mu(E)=\mu(E\cap B)+ \int_{E\setminus B} g(x)\,d\hat\lambda(x)
  \end{equation}
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Choose an usco map $\phi:\mathcal{N}\to X$ with $\phi(\mathcal{N})=N$ put
  \[\hat N:= \{\hat\lambda: \lambda\in \mathcal{P}(\phi(\mathcal{N}_\sigma))\text{ for some $\sigma\in\mathcal{N}$}\}\]
  and recall that $\hat N$ is convexly analytic by \Cref{a1}.
  
  Let $\mathcal{U}$ be the collection of Baire sets $U\subset X$ for which there is $\hat\nu\in\widehat{N}$
  such that $\hat\nu(V)\ne 0$ for every Baire set $V\subset U$ with $\mu(V)\ne 0$. Choose $U_i\in\mathcal{U}$
  for which $|\mu|(U)$, where $U:=\bigcup_i U_i$, is largest possible and let $\hat\nu_i\in\widehat{N}$ be the corresponding measures.
  
  Define $\hat\mu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ by $\hat\mu(E):=\mu(E\setminus U)$.
  Then $\hat\mu\perp\hat\nu$ for every $\hat\nu\in\widehat{N}$. Hence by \Cref{T-2} there is a Baire set $B\subset X\setminus U$ such that
  $|\hat\mu|(X\setminus B)=0$ and $|\nu|(B)=0$ for every $\nu\in N$,
  hence also $|\hat\nu|(B)=0$ for every $\hat\nu\in\hat N$.

  For each $i$ there is a choice $g_i$ of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the absolutely continuous part of $\hat\nu_i$ with respect to $\mu$
  such that $g_i(x)=0$ for $x\in B$.
  By definition of $\widehat{N}$,
  $\hat\nu_i$ is a barycenter of some $\lambda_i\in\mathcal{P}(N)$ with compact support.
  Since
  $\|\nu\|$ is bounded on the support of $\lambda_i$, there are $\kappa_i>0$ such that
  $\kappa_i\int\|\nu\|\,d\lambda_i(\nu)\le 2^{-i}$ and $\kappa_i\int|g_i(x)|\,d|\mu|(x)<2^{-i}$.

  Put $V:=\{x\in U: \sum_i \kappa_i |g_i(x)| <\infty\}$. Then $\mu(U\setminus V)=0$, and hence
  $h_i(x):=g_i(x)$ for $x\in V$ and $h_i(x):=0$ for $x\notin V$ is also
  the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the absolutely continuous part of $\hat\nu_i$ with respect to $\mu$.
  
  Given $t\in[0,1]^{\mathbb{N}}$ we let $\lambda_t:=\sum_i\kappa_i t_i \lambda_i$ and observe that
  $\int\|\nu\|\,d\lambda_t(\nu)\le 1$, the barycenter of $\lambda_t$ is $\nu_t:=\sum_i\kappa_i t_i \nu_i$,
  and the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the absolutely continuous part of $\nu_t$ with respect to $\mu$ is
  the function $g_t$ defined by $g_t(x):=\sum_i\kappa_i t_i g_i(x)$ for $x\in V$ and $g_t(x)=0$ otherwise.
  When $x\in V\cap U_j$ and $t_i$, $i\ne j$, are fixed, there is at most one value
  of $t_j$ such that $g_t(x)=0$. Hence $\Lambda\{t: g_t(x)=0\}$, where $\Lambda$ is the product Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]^\mathbb{N}$,
  and so $\mu\{x\in V\cap U_j: g_t(x)=0\}=0$ for $\Lambda$ almost every $t$ by the Fubini theorem.
  It follows that there is $t\in (0,1]^\mathbb{N}$ such that $g_t(x)\ne 0$ for $\mu$ almost every $x\in V$.
  Fix such a $t$, choose $c>0$ such that $\lambda:=c\lambda_t \in\mathcal{P}(N)$ and put
  \[h(x):=
    \begin{cases}
      1 &\text{when $x\in V$ and $g_t(x)=0$,}\\
       h(x):=cg_t(x)& \text{for all other $x$.}
    \end{cases}
  \]    

  Let $W:=\{x\in V: g_t(x)\ne 0\}$. The restrictions of $\hat\lambda$ and $\mu$ to $W$ are mutually absolutely continuous.
  Since for every $E\subset W$, $\hat\lambda(E)=\int_E cg_t(x)\,d\mu(x)$, we get
  $\mu(E)=\int_E g(x)\,d\hat\lambda(x)$ where $g(x):=1/(cg_t(x))$ for $x\in W$. Letting $g(x)=0$ otherwise, and
  writing $|\hat\lambda|=h\lambda$ where $|h|=1$, we get
  \[\int_X |g(x)|\,d|\hat\lambda|(x)=\int_W h(x)|g(x)|/g(x)\,d\mu(x)<\infty,\]
  and, since $|\hat\lambda|(X\setminus U)=0$ and $|\mu|(U\setminus W)=0$, we see that \eqref{E} holds.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
\label{T-5}
  Let $N\subset\mathcal{M}(X)$ be an analytic set of measures on a complete separable metric space.
  Then for every $\mu\in\mathcal{M}(X)$
  there are 
  a Borel function $g:X\to[0,\infty)$, a Borel set $B\subset X$ and $\lambda\in\mathcal{P}(N)$ such that 
  $g(x)=0$ for $x\in B$,
  $\nu(B)=0$ for every $\nu\in N$ and 
    \[\mu(E)=\mu(E\cap B) + \int_N \int_E g(x)\,d\nu(x)\,d\lambda(\nu)\]
  for every Borel set $E\subset X$.
<!-- end cor-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
As already observed above, for complete separable metric spaces the condition \ref{sm} is automatically satisfied.
  Hence we simply replace the $g$ from \Cref{T-4} by $\max(0,g)$, which is justified 
  by observing that \eqref{E} applied to any set $D\subset\{x: g(x)<0\}$ gives
  $\int_N \int_D g(x)\,d\nu(x)\,d\lambda(\nu)=0$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
Since for every $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_{s}(X)$ and a Baire set $B$ there is a $Z_\sigma$ set $Z\subset B$ such that $|\mu|(B\setminus Z)=0$, 
  the set $B$ in each of the statements of \Cref{T-0} -- \Cref{T-5} can be taken to be $Z_\sigma$.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
